_about: Events and reactor spans for timeline.html. Every entry comes from content/story.md and carries the same source: 'ref' names a reference link defined in story.md, 'href' is a direct link. 'section' is the story heading the event is told under. 'when' is a decimal year used only for placement; 'date' is what is shown. 'label' is a short caption drawn beside the mark.

reactors.name: P
reactors.note: Critical 20 February 1954; down August 1988. Its final shutdown is dated 1988 by SRS and 1991 by OSTI.

reactors.name: L
reactors.note: Running by March 1955; idle from 1968; restarted 1985; down June 1988.

reactors.name: K
reactors.note: Running by March 1955; down April 1988; a test run in 1992, then shut down for good.

reactors.name: C
reactors.note: Running by March 1955; shut down 1985, permanently from 1986.

events.text: Truman writes to Du Pont asking it to build and run the plant
events.section: A site for the hydrogen bomb

events.text: The Savannah River Plant is announced: 250,000 acres, about 1,500 families to move
events.section: A site for the hydrogen bomb
events.label: Plant announced

events.text: Deadline for residents of the first area to leave
Ruth Patrick's baseline survey of the river; the AEC approaches Eugene Odum
Jet reports Black families moving whole houses to New Ellenton
events.label: Houses moved

events.text: The 305-M test pile goes critical; heavy-water production begins
Congress hears that New Ellenton was left out of aid
First shipment of plutonium; the sources disagree on the year
The neutrino is confirmed at P reactor
Odum's survey becomes a permanent laboratory, the Savannah River Ecology Laboratory
Thermal ecology research on the reactors' cooling water begins
The first National Environmental Research Park
events.label: First research park

events.text: The first anti-nuclear protest on the site
Plutonium made lower in Pu-240 to blend with Hanford's, for the buildup
Court rules the L reactor restart needs an environmental impact statement
events.label: Court: L needs an EIS

events.text: A National Academy of Sciences panel reviews reactor safety; Du Pont says it will leave
GAO tells Congress how P reactor's start-up went ahead despite a reactivity shortfall
events.label: GAO on P start-up

events.text: Westinghouse takes over from Du Pont; the Plant becomes the Savannah River Site
The site goes on the National Priorities List
Tritium from K reactor reaches the Savannah River
K reactor's test run, then permanent shutdown: bomb making is over
events.label: Bomb making ends

events.text: The Defense Waste Processing Facility begins turning tank waste into glass
events.label: Waste into glass

events.text: Tanks 17 and 20 closed, the first in the nation
The last spent fuel leaves the receiving basin, closing a forty-year era
The site's laboratory is named the newest national laboratory
Section 3116 settles what tank waste may stay in the ground
House Science Committee hearing on the ecology laboratory's funding cut
Historic markers for P and R, the first inside the fence
P and R reactors sealed in place with Recovery Act money
events.label: P and R sealed

events.text: Ribbon-cutting for the SRS Museum in Aiken
The 4,000th canister of glass, of about 8,000 expected
DOE puts the MOX plant at $17.17 billion, finished in 2048
The Fourth Circuit lifts the injunction keeping MOX alive
events.label: MOX ends

events.text: DOE decides to make plutonium pits at Savannah River
events.label: Pits decided

events.text: SRS.GOV and SRNL.GOV become Archive-It seeds
Tank 14 becomes the eighth old-style tank to finish waste removal in under two years
